newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil cargoes off on quiet day.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil cargoes off on quiet day.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil cargo prices slid below $80 a tonne on Monday on a quiet day with both buyers and sellers relaxed.
The high sulphur low came on the back of a late Friday trade to an Irish utility of 25,000 tonnes at a price heard to be $79.50 a tonne.
Another cargo of high sulphur fuel was heard to have been bought from Scandinavia on Friday at an undisclosed price.
Most traders said there was little to stop the price dwindling further, though a few suggested sellers would resist large drops in value below the $80 mark.
"There are a couple of suppliers out there trying to sell oil but maybe not at the same low numbers (as traded on Friday)," said one.
High sulphur fuel barge prices firmed with trades done at $84.50 and $85. Traders said one buyer was bidding up the market on a very quiet day.
Low sulphur prices firmed notionally with a scarcity of material for prompt delivery boosting values above swap levels.
But traders were sceptical there was real heart in the market, with fresh supplies due soon and trans-atlantic prices undercutting Europe.
